title: Zechariah 5 — The flying scroll and the woman in the ephah

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: wāʾāšûḇ wāʾeśśāʾ ʿênay wāʾerʾeh wəhinnēh məḡillâ ʿāp̄â: šûḇ + verb 'again' (ASV), with KJV 'I turned' reported. Disputed 'scroll' (ASV 'roll') is a register update matching ezekiel-woh 2:9. The reception note quotes TBWTT ch. 3 ('Then I turned ... a flying roll ... twenty cubits (9 meters) ... ten cubits (4.50 meters)') accurately, labels it, and records the KJV/ASV difference. The line gives the scroll no other identity.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: ʾorkāh ʿeśrîm bāʾammâ wəroḥbāh ʿeśer bāʾammâ: the cubits are kept in the line, and the metric equivalents and the parallel with the 1 Kgs 6:3 porch are in commentary. Exact.

zōʾṯ hāʾālâ hayyôṣēʾṯ ʿal-pənê ḵol-hāʾāreṣ ... mizzeh kāmôhā niqqâ: the ASV 'cut off ... on the one side' is kept, and 'the whole land' (central eretz) is correct for Judah. Non-blocking: the note's "'purged away' (NRSV-type)" is loose, since NRSV itself has 'cut off'. Attribute the 'cleaned out / purged' sense of Niphal nqh to the lexicon or a commentator instead.
hôṣēʾṯîhā nəʾum YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ ... wəḵillattû wəʾeṯ-ʿēṣāyw wəʾeṯ-ʾăḇānāyw: the prophetic perfect is rendered 'I will send it out' (ASV). Exact.
wayyēṣēʾ hammalʾāḵ haddōḇēr bî ... śāʾ nāʾ ʿênêḵā ...: exact.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, AB 25B, ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: zōʾṯ hāʾêp̄â hayyôṣēʾṯ ... zōʾṯ ʿênām bəḵol-hāʾāreṣ: the MT ʿênām is rendered by its sense 'their appearance' (ASV), and the LXX/Syriac 'their iniquity' is reported. Exact.
wəhinnēh kikkar ʿōp̄ereṯ niśśēʾṯ wəzōʾṯ ʾiššâ ʾaḥaṯ yôšeḇeṯ ...: exact.
zōʾṯ hārišʿâ ... ʾeḇen hāʿōp̄ereṯ ʾel-pîhā: the ASV personification 'Wickedness' is kept and the article reported; defensible for a figure who acts.

šəttayim nāšîm yôṣəʾôṯ wərûaḥ bəḵanp̄êhem ... kəḵanp̄ê haḥăsîḏâ ... bên hāʾāreṣ ûḇên haššāmāyim: indefinite 'wind', 'stork' and the merism 'between the earth and the skies' are all literal. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3 ('there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings ...'; 'autonomous flight suits') and is labelled; the line describes the figures only as the Hebrew does.

Approve. 'flying scroll', the cubits, 'again' (GKC §120d) and the 1 Kgs 6:3 porch parallel are accurate, and the canon's 'flying craft' is confined to a labelled note.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 11 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (5:1 (with 5:2), 5:9) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: וָאָשׁ֕וּב וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֖י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה מְגִלָּ֥ה עָפָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a flying scroll.

notes.official:
*wāʾāšûḇ wāʾeśśāʾ ʿênay wāʾerʾeh* 'Then again I lifted up my eyes and saw': *šûḇ* followed by a second verb expresses repetition (GKC §120d), as the ASV renders it; the KJV's 'Then I turned', which the canon's English quotes, takes it as a separate movement. *wəhinnēh məḡillâ ʿāp̄â* 'and behold, a flying scroll': *məḡillâ* is the rolled writing-sheet, 'scroll' under the corpus ruling (`megillah-scroll-latter-prophets`; ezekiel-woh 2:9; isaiah-woh 29:11), replacing the draft's ASV 'roll' (overlay `megillah-afah-flying-scroll-zechariah-5`). Chapter conventions: `house-conventions-latter-prophets`.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes 5:1-2 ('Then I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a flying roll ... the length thereof twenty cubits ... and the breadth thereof ten cubits') as 'the description of a flying craft', adding the dimensions in metres. The line renders *məḡillâ ʿāp̄â* 'a flying scroll', the object that v3 explains as a written curse, and gives it no other identity.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ מְגִלָּ֣ה עָפָ֔ה אָרְכָּהּ֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרָחְבָּ֖הּ עֶ֥שֶׂר בָּאַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its breadth ten cubits."

notes.official: *ʾorkāh ʿeśrîm bāʾammâ wəroḥbāh ʿeśer bāʾammâ* 'its length is twenty cubits, and its breadth ten cubits', about 9 by 4.5 metres at the common cubit of about 45 cm. These are the dimensions of the porch of Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:3), which some commentators take as a sign that the curse goes out from the sanctuary. The line keeps the cubits (overlay `megillah-afah-flying-scroll-zechariah-5`; `megillah-scroll-latter-prophets`). The canon's quotation of this verse is noted at v1.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֹ֚את הָֽאָלָ֔ה הַיּוֹצֵ֖את עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י כָל־הַגֹּנֵ֗ב מִזֶּה֙ כָּמ֣וֹהָ נִקָּ֔ה וְכָל־הַנִּ֨שְׁבָּ֔ע מִזֶּ֖ה כָּמ֥וֹהָ נִקָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Then he said to me, "This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole land; for everyone who steals shall be cut off on the one side according to it, and everyone who swears shall be cut off on the other side according to it.

notes.official: *zōʾṯ hāʾālâ* 'This is the curse': *ʾālâ* is the sworn sanction of a covenant (Deut 29:19-20), written on the scroll. It goes out 'over the face of the whole land' (central `eretz`), the land of Judah. *mizzeh ... mizzeh* 'on the one side ... on the other side' is usually taken of the two sides of the scroll, one for thieves and one for perjurers (ASV); others render 'from here'. *niqqâ* 'shall be cut off' (ASV; NRSV likewise 'cut off') is disputed: the verb *nqh* means 'be clean, be free (of guilt or punishment)', and some render 'has gone unpunished' (NJPS), in which case the curse is the remedy for crime that went unpunished. The line keeps the ASV (overlay `megillah-afah-flying-scroll-zechariah-5`).

paragraphs.text: הוֹצֵאתִ֗יהָ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבָ֙אָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַגַּנָּ֔ב וְאֶל־בֵּ֛ית הַנִּשְׁבָּ֥ע בִּשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וְלָ֙נֶה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ בֵּית֔וֹ וְכִלַּ֖תּוּ וְאֶת־עֵצָ֥יו וְאֶת־אֲבָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: I will send it out, declares YHWH of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him who swears falsely by my name; and it shall lodge in the midst of his house and shall consume it, with its timber and its stones."

notes.official: *hôṣēʾṯîhā nəʾum YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ* 'I will send it out, declares YHWH of hosts' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). *wəlānâ bəṯôḵ bêṯô wəḵillattû* 'and it shall lodge in the midst of his house and shall consume it': the curse destroys the house of the thief and of the one who swears falsely by YHWH's name (Ex 20:7, 15; Lev 19:11-12), down to its timber and stones (cf. Lev 14:45). The messenger's explanation, opened in v3, closes here (overlay `megillah-afah-flying-scroll-zechariah-5`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֕א הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מָ֖ה הַיּוֹצֵ֥את הַזֹּֽאת׃

i18n.en: Then the messenger who talked with me went out and said to me, "Lift up now your eyes, and see what this is that goes out."

notes.official: *wayyēṣēʾ hammalʾāḵ haddōḇēr bî* 'Then the messenger who talked with me went out' (overlay `hammalakh-haddover-bi-interpreting-messenger-zechariah`; central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`). The seventh vision (5:5-11) begins (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`).

paragraphs.text: וָאֹמַ֖ר מַה־הִ֑יא וַיֹּ֗אמֶר זֹ֤את הָֽאֵיפָה֙ הַיּוֹצֵ֔את וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֹ֥את עֵינָ֖ם בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah that goes out." And he said, "This is their appearance in all the land."

notes.official: *zōʾṯ hāʾêp̄â hayyôṣēʾṯ* 'This is the ephah that goes out': the *ʾêp̄â* is a dry measure of about 22 litres and the basket that holds it (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`). *zōʾṯ ʿênām bəḵol-hāʾāreṣ* 'This is their appearance in all the land': the MT has *ʿênām* 'their eye', rendered by its sense with the ASV; the Old Greek and Syriac read *ʿăwōnām* 'their iniquity' (NRSV), and the MT is kept (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). 'the land' is Judah, from which the wickedness is removed (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֛ה כִּכַּ֥ר עֹפֶ֖רֶת נִשֵּׂ֑את וְזֹאת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאֵיפָֽה׃

i18n.en: And behold, a talent of lead was lifted up; and this is a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.

notes.official: *kikkar ʿōp̄ereṯ* 'a talent of lead': a round lid of lead weighing a talent, lifted to show the woman inside. *ʾiššâ ʾaḥaṯ yôšeḇeṯ* 'a woman sitting' in the ephah (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ זֹ֣את הָרִשְׁעָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הָֽאֵיפָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֛ךְ אֶת־אֶ֥בֶן הָעֹפֶ֖רֶת אֶל־פִּֽיהָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he said, "This is Wickedness." And he cast her down into the midst of the ephah, and he cast the weight of lead upon its mouth.

notes.official: *zōʾṯ hārišʿâ* 'This is Wickedness': the Hebrew has the article, 'the wickedness'; the ASV's personified 'Wickedness' is kept, since the figure is a woman pushed back into the basket (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`). *ʾeḇen hāʿōp̄ereṯ* 'the weight of lead', literally 'the stone of lead', is the lid of v7, cast on the ephah's mouth.

paragraphs.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֨א עֵינַ֜י וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּה֩ שְׁתַּ֨יִם נָשִׁ֤ים יֽוֹצְאוֹת֙ וְר֣וּחַ בְּכַנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָהֵ֥נָּה כְנָפַ֖יִם כְּכַנְפֵ֣י הַחֲסִידָ֑ה וַתִּשֶּׂ֙אנָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵיפָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֵ֥ין הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, two women came out, and wind was in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of a stork; and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the skies.

notes.official:
*šəttayim nāšîm yôṣəʾôṯ wərûaḥ bəḵanp̄êhem* 'two women came out, and wind was in their wings': *rûaḥ* is physical wind and has no article in the Hebrew (`ruach-spirit-wind-breath-latter-prophets`; ASV 'the wind'). The masculine suffix on 'wings' (*-hem*) for the women is a common neutralization of gender. *kəḵanp̄ê haḥăsîḏâ* 'like the wings of a stork', a large migratory bird with broad wings (Lev 11:19; Jer 8:7). *bên hāʾāreṣ ûḇên haššāmāyim* 'between the earth and the skies': the merism for the whole space between ground and sky (cf. 1 Chr 21:16), rendered 'earth' in its cosmic scope (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`) and 'skies' in the physical register (central `shamayim`), replacing the draft's 'the land' (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`). ezekiel-woh 8:3 has 'between the land and the skies' under its own convention.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork') and reads the two as female companions of the creators, equipped with autonomous flight suits, appearing for the first time. The line describes the two women only as the Hebrew does.

paragraphs.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י אָ֛נָה הֵ֥מָּה מֽוֹלִכ֖וֹת אֶת־הָאֵיפָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then I said to the messenger who talked with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"

notes.official: *ʾānâ hēmmâ môliḵôṯ ʾeṯ-hāʾêp̄â* 'Where are they taking the ephah?' (overlay `hammalakh-haddover-bi-interpreting-messenger-zechariah`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י לִבְנֽוֹת־לָ֥הֿ בַ֖יִת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁנְעָ֑ר וְהוּכַ֛ן וְהֻנִּ֥יחָה שָּׁ֖ם עַל־מְכֻנָתָֽהּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he said to me, "To build her a house in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared, she shall be set there on her own base."

notes.official: *liḇnôṯ-lāh ḇayiṯ bəʾereṣ šinʿār* 'To build her a house in the land of Shinar': Shinar is the old name of Babylonia (Gen 10:10; 11:2; central `eretz-shinar`), and the 'house' is a temple. The edition prints *lāh* 'for her' with a rafe over the final he, marking the absence of the mappiq the suffix normally carries; the form is the third-feminine suffix and is translated 'for her' (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). *wəhûḵan wəhunnîḥâ šām ʿal-məḵunāṯāh* 'and when it is prepared, she shall be set there on her own base': *məḵunâ* is the stand or pedestal of a cult object (cf. Ezra 3:3; 1 Kgs 7:27), so the wickedness is installed like an idol in Babylon, as the commentaries generally read it; ASV 'in her own place' (overlay `ephah-rishah-woman-in-the-ephah-zechariah-5`).
